Group 2 elements, also known as alkaline earth metals, include Be, Mg, Ca, Sr, Ba, and Ra. Typically, as you move down the group from Be to Ra, the atomic mass increases, and so does the size of the atoms. This can affect their densities. Generally, for group 2 elements, the density tends to increase as you go down the group due to the increase in atomic mass being more significant than the increase in atomic volume. Therefore, the density of these elements usually increases from Be to Ra.
